title: The Market for AI-Assisted Signaling
abstract: arXiv:2611.02910v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: This paper studies a market in which AI providers choose technologies and prices for assistance used to signal ability. Individual adoption is unobserved. Profitable assistance can lower welfare relative to signaling without AI, even when ability remains fully revealed. Easier imitation increases the output required to demonstrate ability, and the extra signaling can outweigh production savings. Providers can profit from improving assistance for lower-ability senders because this increases higher-ability senders' purchases. Such improvements can lower welfare relative to retaining existing tools. Competition among providers offering the same technology supports full information, but development costs can sustain monopoly provision that conceals ability. Greater verification capacity can also reduce information by changing which customers providers serve.

translated_abstract: 本文研究了一个市场，其中AI提供商为用作能力信号的辅助服务选择技术和价格。个体的采用行为是无法被观测的。即使能力仍然被完全揭示，有利可图的AI辅助相对于没有AI的信号传递也可能降低社会福利。更容易的模仿会增加展示能力所需的产出量，而额外的信号传递成本可能超过生产上的节省。提供商可以通过改善针对低能力发送者的辅助服务来获利，因为这会增加高能力发送者的购买。此类改进相对于保留现有工具而言可能降低社会福利。提供相同技术的提供商之间的竞争支持完全信息披露，但开发成本可能维持掩盖能力的垄断供给。更大的验证能力也可能通过改变提供商所服务的客户群体而减少信息。
tldr: 本文研究了AI辅助能力信号传递市场，发现即使能力被完全揭示，有利可图的AI辅助也可能降低社会福利，且提供商可通过改善低能力用户的辅助服务获利，但这类改进反而可能损害整体福利。
en_tdlr: This paper studies a market for AI-assisted ability signaling, showing that profitable AI assistance can lower welfare even when ability is fully revealed, and providers may profit from improving assistance for lower-ability senders while such improvements reduce overall welfare.
